sections.content: [Placeholder passage text about polar bears: Liu and colleagues studied polar bear genetics by comparing different groups of polar bears (not the first to compare with brown bears genetically). Polar bears have high fat intake but don't suffer health problems — they control 'bad' cholesterol by genetic means. Female polar bears survive about 6 months without food during denning. Bones of female polar bears remain strong when emerging in spring. The bone-density mechanism could one day help humans. Bears are considered unintelligent and 'aggressive' but may not be — Tennoji Zoo bear used branch as a tool to knock down food/objects; wild polar bear figured out how to reach a platform with a camera/food/something located on it; bears display conscious manipulation of objects and game-like play behaviour; may display frustration when hunting; may form relationships with other species.]

sections.content: [Placeholder passage text about AI and work: AI will change the nature of work for many people. Stella Pachidi (Cambridge Judge Business School) studies 'algorithmication' of knowledge-economy jobs; the knowledge economy is a key driver of workplace developments. She observed staff at a telecom company allowing AI to carry out tasks they should do themselves. Hamish Low argues greater automation won't cause lower employment; several reasons AI appeals to businesses; AI's potential resembles past cultural shifts (like industrial revolution). Ewan McGaughey's research shows how job market changes can be successfully handled; governments/authorities should ensure adequately paid work for all; workers will follow less conventional career paths. Researchers working on making AI decision-making more transparent to build user confidence/trust.]
